Learning Objectives

By the end of this session you will be able to:

  1. - Open an unfamiliar dataset in pandas and answer the first four questions about it.
  2. - Classify a column by measurement scale, and choose an analysis that the scale permits.
  3. - State the IID assumption in plain words and test whether a dataset honours it.
  4. - Work the loop: Analysis, Issue, Tools, Solution, and present the result so someone else can check it.

  • Nobody trains a model on data they have not looked at.

Three People, Four Things We Know About Them

PersonHeight_cmAgeShoe_sizeLikes_coffee
Ana1682238yes

  • One column is one thing measured on every person, in the same unit, all the way down.
  • Person is a name tag, not a measurement. The measurements are Height_cm, Age and Shoe_size.
DefinitionA dataset is a rectangle. Rows are the things you observed, columns are the properties you recorded about all of them.

What You Predict, and What You Predict It From

  • Pick the column you want to predict. That one choice splits the table in two.
Statistics calls itMachine learning calls itIn our table
independent variablesfeatures, inputs, XHeight_cm, Age, Shoe_size
dependent variabletarget, label, yLikes_coffee
  • The dependent variable is the one whose value depends on the others. That is the whole name.
  • Nothing in a file marks which column is the label. You choose it, and the choice defines the problem.

The File Has No Header, So You Name the Columns

  • The .txt files have no header row. The .arff twin does, so take the names from there.
arff = open(os.path.join(path, "KDDTrain+.arff"))
NAMES = [l.split()[1].strip("'") for l in arff if l.lower().startswith("@attribute")]
COLS  = NAMES[:41] + ["class", "difficulty"]   # 41 features, then the label, then metadata
train = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(path, "KDDTrain+.txt"), names=COLS)
test  = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(path, "KDDTest+.txt"),  names=COLS)
print(len(COLS), train.shape, test.shape)
What you should see
43 (125973, 43) (22544, 43)
Watch outSkip names= and pandas eats the first connection as a header: one row short, nonsense names.
TipEvery column and its measured range: verified NSL-KDD column reference.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
11

Build the family Column Yourself

  • The file gives you the attack name. It does not group them. That grouping is yours to make.
FAMILY = {"neptune": "DoS", "satan": "Probe", "guess_passwd": "R2L",
          "buffer_overflow": "U2R", ...}          # 22 names in training

for df in (train, test):
    df["family"] = df["class"].apply(
        lambda c: "Normal" if c == "normal" else FAMILY.get(c, "UNKNOWN"))

print(train["family"].value_counts())
  • Four families: DoS, Probe, R2L, U2R. Normal traffic is its own label.
Watch outCheck for UNKNOWN before you trust the grouping. An attack name you did not map is a silent hole in every count that follows.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
12

Two Formats, Two Column Counts

  • The class found this: KDDTest+.arff declares 42 attributes, KDDTest+.txt has 43 columns.
  • Two differences, not one. The ARFF drops difficulty, and its class attribute is {normal, anomaly}, so the 37 attack names are gone with it.
  • No family column can be built from the ARFF, and no novel-attack analysis either.
Why it mattersTwo files, same dataset, different shape. This is why the first thing you print is the shape, and why a column count that surprises you is a finding rather than an annoyance.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems

Counting the Columns Before You Trust Either File

txt  = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(path, "KDDTest+.txt"), names=COLS)
arff = [l for l in open(os.path.join(path, "KDDTest+.arff")) if l.lower().startswith("@attribute")]
print(txt.shape[1], "columns in the txt")
print(len(arff), "attributes declared in the arff")
print(arff[-1])   # the class attribute: look at what it holds
  • Tools: count columns before trusting either file. An ARFF header names its attributes, so it is also a free check on the names you imported.
  • Solution: we always work from the .txt files. Read the ARFF header to confirm a spelling, never to load the data.

What You Are Holding

  • read_csv hands you a DataFrame. Think of a spreadsheet that Python can talk to.
  • Rows are records. Here, one row is one network connection.
  • Columns are named, and each column has one type for the whole column.
train.shape       # (rows, columns)
train.columns     # the column names
train["duration"] # one column, called a Series
train.head(3)     # the first three rows
AnalogyA DataFrame is a spreadsheet tab. A Series is a single column of it. Everything today is one of those two things.

15

The First Four Questions

  • How big is it, and what are the columns?
  • What type is each column, and does that type make sense?
  • What is missing, and is missing meaningful?
  • What does the thing I am predicting actually look like?
  1. 1train.shape gives rows and columns.
  2. 2train.dtypes gives the type pandas guessed. It guesses.
  3. 3train.isna().sum() counts missing values per column.
  4. 4train["class"].value_counts() shows the target.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
16

What info() Tells You, and What It Hides

train.info(show_counts=True)
  • Non-null counts per column, so missing data is visible.
  • The dtype pandas inferred: int64, float64, object.
  • object almost always means text, which means a decision is waiting for you.
Watch outdtypes is a guess from the file, not a statement about meaning. A column of 0s and 1s is int64 whether it counts bytes or flags a yes/no.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
17

describe() and Its Blind Spot

train.describe().T[["mean", "50%", "max"]]
  • Only numeric columns appear, so text columns silently vanish from the summary.
  • The mean of a skewed column is not a typical value.
  • For src_bytes, mean is about 45,567 while the median is 44.
Why it mattersThe mean is dragged by a handful of enormous connections. Report the median for skewed data, and always look at the maximum.
NoteBook section 3.5, Analyzing and Visualizing Datasets, runs this same summary step on other data. Read it in MindTap after class.

Look At It, Do Not Just Summarize It

  • Two columns can share a mean and look nothing alike. Plot before you conclude.
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
sns.countplot(data=train, x="family")            # how many rows per class
plt.show()
sns.histplot(np.log1p(train["src_bytes"]), bins=50)   # log scale, or you see one bar
plt.show()
  • countplot for categories, histplot for numbers, boxplot when you want outliers to stand out.
  • np.log1p is log(1 + x), which is safe when the column contains zeros.
TipA histogram that is one tall spike is a finding, not a broken plot: the column needs a transform.
NoteBook section 3.5 also covers matching a chart to a column.

Know What Kind of Number You Have

  • The scale of a column decides which statistics are even defined for it.
  • Get this wrong and you can compute a number that means nothing.

The Four Measurement Scales

ScaleWhat it supportsCentreExample here
Nominallabels only, no ordermodeprotocol_type, service, flag
Ordinalranked, gaps not equalmode, mediana severity rank, a Likert answer
Intervalequal gaps, no true zeromeantemperature in C, calendar year
Ratioequal gaps, real zeromean, ratiosduration, src_bytes, count
  • Ratio has a true zero, so "twice as many bytes" is a sentence that means something.
  • Interval does not, so "twice as warm" is not.

21

One Correction to the Reading

  • The blog groups interval under qualitative data. That is wrong.
  • Interval data is quantitative: it is numeric with equal spacing, it just lacks a true zero.
  • Qualitative is nominal and ordinal. Quantitative is interval and ratio.
  • Use the reading for the examples, use this slide for the classification.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
22

Discrete and Continuous Is a Different Question

  • Nominal, ordinal, interval, ratio describe what the values mean. This deck uses three chapters: nominal, ordinal, and amounts.
  • Discrete and continuous describe what values are possible, and they are how the amounts chapter is split.
  • count is ratio and discrete: whole connections, never 2.5 of them.
  • duration is ratio and continuous: any value in a range.
DefinitionDiscrete means countable in whole units. Continuous means you can always divide the interval further, at least in principle.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems

Nominal Columns: Categories, Not Amounts

  • One data type at a time. First the nominal columns: what they are, which columns of NSL-KDD they are, and the three things slide 25 lets you compute on them: counts, the mode, chi-square.
  • Every number in this chapter comes from KDDTrain+, all 125,973 rows, unless the slide says otherwise.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
26

Nominal in Plain Words

DefinitionA nominal column holds categories: eye colour, nationality, the make of a car. Its values are labels you can tell apart, not amounts you can add.
  • The test: could you sort the values from smallest to largest? If the question makes no sense, the column is nominal.
  • What you can do: count how many rows carry each value, find the most common value, and ask whether the value is related to the label.
  • What you cannot do: average them. There is no value halfway between tcp and udp.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems

service70http, private, domain_uthe destination service
flag11SF, S0, REJhow the connection ended
five yes/no columns2 each0, 1no or yes; 0 and 1 are values, not amounts
class23normal, neptune, smurfthe label
  • The five yes/no columns are land, logged_in, root_shell, is_host_login, is_guest_login. Nine nominal columns in all.
  • Not nominal: hot, num_failed_logins and the other counts. Those are amounts, for the amounts chapter.

Mode: The Most Common Value

DefinitionThe mode is the value with the largest count. It is the only typical value a nominal column has, because there is no middle to average.
  • All rows: protocol_type tcp, service http, flag SF, and 0 for every yes/no column.
  • Split by the label the mode moves. A group is the rows of one label: the 67,343 normal rows, or the 58,630 attack rows. Normal rows are http and SF, a finished web request; attack rows are private and S0, a SYN to a private port that nobody answered.
  • What it tells you: when the most common value differs between the two groups, the column can tell them apart. Chi-square measures exactly that, next.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
33

Mode, Twice on NSL-KDD

  • Group means attack rows or normal rows; only the five most common values are shown.

Chi-Square, Step 1: The Question, the Rows and the Label

  • The question: is protocol_type related to whether a row is an attack?
  • The rows: all 125,973 rows of KDDTrain+. Nothing is filtered out. KDDTest+ is not touched; it is the exam.
  • The label: class has 23 values in KDDTrain+. Keep normal as normal; every other value becomes attack. Two values, normal and attack.
  • The pair: one nominal column against the two-value label.
Tip"Against the label" on every slide that follows means this: every row of KDDTrain+, class collapsed to normal or attack.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems

Chi-Square, Step 3: The Table Chance Would Give (What We Expected)

  • If protocol had nothing to do with attacks, every protocol would carry the file's attack share, 46.5 percent.
  • Expected count = row total x column total / grand total. For icmp and attack: 8,291 x 58,630 / 125,973 = 3,858.8.
protocol_typenormal, expectedattack, expected
icmp4,432.23,858.8
tcp54,895.847,793.2
udp8,015.06,978.0
  • Compare with step 2: icmp has 6,982 attacks where chance would give 3,859. That gap is what the test measures.

Chi-Square, Step 4: The Statistic

  • For each of the six cells: (observed minus expected) squared, divided by expected. Then add the six.
cellobservedexpectedterm
icmp, normal1,3094,432.22,200.8
icmp, attack6,9823,858.82,527.9
tcp, normal53,60054,895.830.6
tcp, attack49,08947,793.235.1
udp, normal12,4348,015.02,436.4
udp, attack2,5596,978.02,798.4
  • Chi-square = 10,029.2. In words: how far the real table is from the chance table. Zero would mean no relationship at all.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
38

Chi-Square, Step 5: Degrees of Freedom

DefinitionThe degrees of freedom of a table is how many cells you can fill in freely once the totals are known. For r rows and c columns it is (r minus 1) times (c minus 1).
  • Our table has 3 rows and 2 columns: 2 times 1 = 2. Fill in icmp-attack and tcp-attack, and every other cell is forced: the row totals fix icmp-normal and tcp-normal, the column totals fix both udp cells.
  • What it is for: luck produces small chi-square values, and how small depends on the size of the table. A 2 by 2 table has one free cell and luck stays under 3.8 nineteen times in twenty. Our 3 by 2 table has two, and luck stays under 6.0. The flag table, 11 by 2, has ten, and luck reaches 18.3.
  • So the degrees of freedom picks the curve luck follows, and the next step reads the p-value off that curve.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
39

Two Free Cells, and the Curve They Choose

  • Left, the real table with the two cells you can choose in green. Right, what luck alone produces, for three sizes of table.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
40

Chi-Square, Step 6: The p-Value, in Plain Words

DefinitionSuppose protocol_type had nothing to do with attacks. Then the observed table would differ from the expected table only by luck. The p-value is how often luck alone makes chi-square at least as big as the one we got.
  • How to get it by hand: scramble the attack label so it means nothing, rebuild the table, recompute chi-square, and repeat 1,000 times. Count how many of the 1,000 reach the real value. That share is the p-value.
  • How the computer gets it: from the curve luck follows for our degrees of freedom. With 2, luck stays under 6.0 nineteen times in twenty. Our chi-square is 10,029, so p is below 0.001: luck practically never does this.
  • What it does not say: how strong the relationship is. On 125,973 rows almost every column gets p below 0.001, so p cannot rank columns; that is what Cramer's V is for.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems

The p-Value, Shown by Scrambling the Label

  • The grey bars are 1,000 chi-squares computed with a scrambled label; the red line is the real one. Same file, all rows.

columnvalueschi-squaredegrees of freedom
protocol_type310,0292

  • service has the largest number, and it also has 70 values and 69 degrees of freedom. The statistic grows with the number of rows and with the number of values, not only with the strength of the relationship.
  • So no: you cannot say service beats flag from these numbers. You need one scale.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
44

Chi-Square, Step 8: Cramer's V Puts Every Column on One Scale

DefinitionCramer's V is chi-square rescaled by the number of rows and the size of the table: the square root of chi-square divided by (rows times (k minus 1)), where k is the smaller of the table's two dimensions.
  • Here k is 2 for every column, because the label has two values. So V is the square root of chi-square divided by 125,973.
  • protocol_type: the square root of 10,029 divided by 125,973 is 0.282.
  • 0 means no relationship; 1 means the column tells you the label exactly. Values from different columns are comparable. Rule of thumb: below 0.1 small, around 0.3 medium, above 0.5 large.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems

is_guest_login, root_shell, land, is_host_login0.039 and belowdrop

Reading the Attack-Share Figure

  • For each value, attack share = attack rows with that value / all rows with that value. For flag SF it is 15 percent, so 85 percent of SF rows are normal.
  • The dashed line is the whole file: 47 percent of all 125,973 rows are attacks. A value far from that line is a value that tells the two groups apart.
  • S0 at 99 percent and SF at 15 are far from 47 in opposite directions. That spread is what makes V large.
  • Everything on the figure is KDDTrain+, all rows, class collapsed to normal or attack.

Why You May Not Average a Nominal Column

  • Code protocol_type as tcp 0, udp 1, icmp 2 and its mean is 0.25. Code it icmp 0, tcp 1, udp 2 and the mean is 1.05. A number that changes when you rename things is not a measurement.
  • Cramer's V is 0.282 either way, because chi-square counts rows and never looks at what the codes are.
  • The mean of an ordinal column is the same trap: mean difficulty is 19.5, but the step from 20 to 21 is not the step from 2 to 3. Report the median.
TipThe right-hand column of slide 25 is not a rule about statistics. It is a rule about what a number can mean when the values were never amounts.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
51

Nominal, Summed Up

  1. 1Analysis: counts and the mode for every nominal column, all rows and per label.
  2. 2Issue: 15 rare service values; four yes/no columns that are almost always 0.
  3. 3Tools: chi-square against the label, degrees of freedom, p, then Cramer's V so the columns share one scale.
  4. 4Solution: keep service (rare values merged), flag, logged_in, protocol_type. Drop is_guest_login, root_shell, land, is_host_login. Threshold written down: V of 0.1.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
52

Ordinal Columns: Order Without Equal Steps

  • The second data type. What an ordinal column is, why NSL-KDD has none stored as one, the two things in it that behave like one, and the two statistics slide 25 allows: the median and rank tests.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
53

Ordinal in Plain Words

DefinitionAn ordinal column holds names that have an order. T-shirt sizes S, M, L, XL. Satisfaction from 1 to 5. Education level. You can say which is higher, but not by how much.
  • The test: can you sort the values? Yes. Is the step from S to M the same as the step from M to L? No.
  • What you can do: everything a nominal column allows, plus the median (the middle value) and rank tests (compare positions).
  • What you cannot do: average them. The mean of S and L is not M, and a satisfaction of 4 is not twice a 2.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
54

The Ordinal Columns of NSL-KDD

  • NSL-KDD stores no column as an ordered set of names. That is common: most tables store ordered things as numbers.
  • Two things in the file behave as ordinal, and this chapter uses both:
  • difficulty, 0 to 21: how many of 21 classifiers got the row right. Ordered, but the step from 20 to 21 does not mean what the step from 2 to 3 means. Metadata, never a feature.
  • Any amount cut into ordered bands: src_bytes as 0, 1 to 100, 101 to 1,000, 1,001 to 10,000, over 10,000. That is binning, and it turns a ratio column into an ordinal one on purpose.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
55

Median: The Middle Value

DefinitionSort the values and take the one in the middle: the median. Half the rows are at or below it. It never looks at how far away the ends are, which is why it works on ordered names.
  • difficulty: median 21 for normal rows, 19 for attack rows. The means are 20.3 and 18.6.
  • src_bytes bands: the median band is 101 to 1,000 for normal rows and 0 for attack rows.
  • What it tells you: the typical attack row was harder for the classifiers, and the typical attack row sent nothing at all.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
56

Rank Test: Compare Positions, Not Values

DefinitionA rank test puts every row of both groups into one sorted list and asks: pick one attack row and one normal row at random; how often is the attack row higher up the list? That share is the answer. 0.5 means the two groups sit together.
  • The process: the two groups are the attack rows and the normal rows of KDDTrain+. scipy.stats.mannwhitneyu(attack_values, normal_values) returns U. The share is U divided by (attack rows times normal rows).
  • src_bytes bands: 0.11. An attack row is higher up only one time in nine. difficulty: 0.24.
  • The p-value is below 0.001 for both, as it is for almost everything on this file. The share is the number that says how much.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
57

Median and Rank Test, Twice on NSL-KDD

  • Left, each band's share of its group. Right, the share of rows at or below each difficulty score, per group.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
58

Which Ordinal Columns to Keep

  • Turn the share into a distance from 0.5: 0.11 is 0.39 away, 0.24 is 0.26 away. Twice that distance is Cliff's delta, the effect size for rank tests: 0.78 and 0.52.
  • Rule of thumb for Cliff's delta: below 0.15 nothing, 0.33 medium, 0.47 large. Both are large.
  • Decision: the src_bytes bands separate the groups strongly and are a feature. difficulty separates them too, and must not be a feature.
Watch outdifficulty was computed from the labels, so a model that sees it is reading the answer key. The slide on where the score came from, later in this deck, shows how.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
59

Amounts: Discrete and Continuous

  • The third data type. What an amount is, discrete or continuous, which columns of NSL-KDD are amounts, and the statistics slide 25 allows: the mean, the standard deviation, the t-test, correlation and regression.
  • Three ideas the statistics need, each with its own slide and graph: the bell shape, the p-value, and effect size.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
60

Amounts in Plain Words: Discrete and Continuous

DefinitionAn amount is a number you can add. A discrete amount is counted in whole units: students in a room, cars in a lot, connections to a host. A continuous amount is measured and can fall anywhere in a range: height, weight, seconds, bytes.
  • The test: can you have two and a half of it? Two and a half connections, no: discrete. Two and a half seconds, yes: continuous.
  • What you can do with either: everything above, plus the mean, the standard deviation, t-tests, correlation and regression. The two kinds share every statistic; they differ in how you draw them, bars for discrete, a histogram for continuous.
  • The zero question, once: statisticians also split amounts into interval (equal steps, no true zero, like temperature in Celsius) and ratio (zero means none, like bytes). Every amount in NSL-KDD is ratio, so that split changes nothing here.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
61

The Amount Columns of NSL-KDD

GroupKindColumnsRange in KDDTrain+
sizes and times, 3continuousduration, src_bytes, dst_bytessrc_bytes 0 to 1,379,963,888
content counts, 11discretehot, num_failed_logins, num_compromised, num_root, num_file_creations, num_shells, num_access_files, num_outbound_cmds, su_attempted, wrong_fragment, urgenthot 0 to 77
window counts, 4discretecount, srv_count, dst_host_count, dst_host_srv_countcount 0 to 511
rates, 15continuousserror_rate through dst_host_srv_rerror_rate0.00 to 1.00
  • Thirty-three amounts: 15 discrete, 18 continuous. The rates are shares, so their mean is a share too. num_outbound_cmds is 0 on every row and says nothing.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
62

Mean: Add Them Up, Divide by the Count

DefinitionThe mean is the total divided by the number of rows. It is the right typical value only when the values pile up in the middle; a few huge values drag it.
  • Example 1, count: mean 155 for attack rows, 23 for normal rows. The column is capped at 511, so there is no tail and the mean is honest.
  • Example 2, serror_rate runs from 0 to 1, so its mean is a share: 0.596 for attack rows, 0.013 for normal. 58 percent of attack rows sit at exactly 1; 0.6 percent of normal rows do.
  • What it says: attack rows hit the same host 155 times in two seconds, on average, and most of those connections fail. That is a SYN flood in two numbers.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
63

Mean, Twice on NSL-KDD

  • Left, two histograms with their means marked. Right, the mean of a 0-to-1 column.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
64

When the Mean Lies: Median for an Amount With a Tail

  • duration: median 0 seconds for attack rows and for normal rows. The means are 423 and 169.
  • 96 percent of attack rows and 88 percent of normal rows last exactly 0 seconds. The means are made by a few long connections.
  • What it tells you: on a column like this the mean describes a handful of rows and the median describes the file. Report the median, and say why.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
65

The Mean Against the Median, Twice on NSL-KDD

  • Left, the middle half and the median of difficulty per family. Right, median against mean for duration.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
66

Standard Deviation: How Far From the Mean, Typically

DefinitionThe standard deviation is the typical distance of a value from the mean. Small: the values sit close to the mean. Larger than the mean: the column has a tail, and the mean is not describing it.
  • Example 1, serror_rate: normal rows mean 0.01, sd 0.09. Attack rows mean 0.60, sd 0.49. The attack rows are two crowds, most at 1 and a large minority at 0.
  • Example 2, src_bytes: mean 45,566 bytes, sd 5,870,331. The sd is 129 times the mean. After log1p: mean 3.2, sd 3.0.
  • What it says: the sd tells you whether the mean can be trusted. On raw src_bytes it cannot; the largest value is 1,379,963,888 bytes.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
67

Standard Deviation, Twice on NSL-KDD

  • Left, each mean with one sd either side. Right, the transformed column with its sd band, and the raw numbers beside it.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
68

What a Bell Shape Is

DefinitionA bell shape is a histogram with one hump in the middle and two matching sides. The mean and the median sit in the same place, and about 68 percent of rows sit within one standard deviation of the mean.
  • Why it matters: the mean, the t-test and Pearson correlation assume roughly this shape. On a bell they are honest; on a long tail they are dragged by the tail.
  • src_bytes is not a bell. Its skewness is 191 raw; a bell has 0. After log1p it is 0.31, closer, but 48 percent of rows sit within one sd instead of 68, and the mean, 3.2, sits left of the median, 3.8.
  • The decision: not bell-shaped, so use the median and rank tests, or transform first and look again.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
69

A Bell, and a Column That Is Not One

  • Left, the shape the tests assume. Right, the real column, with the bell that would have the same mean and sd drawn over it.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
70

The Same Column Raw and After log1p

  • The transform reveals the humps; it does not make a bell.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
71

What a p-Value Is, Shown by Shuffling

DefinitionThe p-value is how often luck alone would make a gap as big as the one you found. Shuffle the labels so they mean nothing, measure the gap again, repeat a thousand times, and count.
  • Column hot, 300 random rows: the real gap between the attack mean and the normal mean is -0.38. In 347 of 1,000 shuffles luck made a gap that big or bigger: p = 0.35. Luck can do it, so the gap means nothing.
  • The same column, all 125,973 rows: the real gap is -0.06. Not one shuffle in a thousand came near it; the largest was 0.04. p is below 0.001. Luck cannot do it.
  • What it tells you: p depends on how many rows you have as much as on the gap. A gap of 0.06 on a column that runs 0 to 77 is real and tiny. That is why the next slides read the effect size after p.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
72

p-Value, Twice on the Same Column

  • The grey bars are what luck did in 1,000 shuffles. The red line is the real gap.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
73

t-Test: Are Two Means Apart by More Than Luck?

DefinitionA t-test compares two means. t is the gap between them divided by the noise you would expect from the two spreads and the two group sizes. A large t means the gap is many times bigger than noise. The p-value comes from t and the degrees of freedom, which here is about the number of rows minus 2.
  • serror_rate: t = 285, p below 0.001. hot: t = -4.7, p below 0.001. Both are real by the test.
  • Cohen's d is the gap measured in spreads: 1.72 for serror_rate, -0.03 for hot. One is huge, the other nothing.
  • What it tells you: with 125,973 rows the t-test calls almost any gap real. Read d: past 0.8 is large, below 0.2 is noise you happen to be able to measure.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
74

t-Test, Twice on NSL-KDD

  • Two means with their 95 percent intervals; the intervals are tiny because the file is large.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
75

Effect Size: Does the Gap Matter?

DefinitionAn effect size says how big a difference is, in units that do not grow with the number of rows. Cohen's d for means: the gap divided by the spread. Cliff's delta for ranks: twice the rank-test share minus one.
  • Rules of thumb: d of 0.2 small, 0.5 medium, 0.8 large. Cliff's delta of 0.15 small, 0.33 medium, 0.47 large.
  • On this file: serror_rate d = 1.72, hot d = -0.03; count delta = 0.64, duration delta = -0.08.
  • The decision rule this deck uses: keep a numeric column when its Cliff's delta against the label is past 0.3, in either direction. Write the threshold down.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
76

Which Columns Actually Separate the Two Groups

  • Nine columns ranked by Cliff's delta, with the 0.3 line the decision uses.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
77

Rank Test on an Amount With a Tail

DefinitionA rank test replaces every value with its position in the sorted list and compares positions. Mann-Whitney U asks: pick one attack row and one normal row at random; how often does the attack row rank higher? That share is the whole answer.
  • Example 1, duration: P(attack ranks higher) = 0.46. The p-value is 0 and the answer is a coin flip.
  • Example 2, count: P(attack ranks higher) = 0.82. Medians 138 against 4.
  • What it says: duration does not separate the groups, whatever the p-value says. count does, strongly. The share is the number to report.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
78

Rank Tests, Twice on NSL-KDD

  • The share of rows at or below each value, per group. The gap between the curves is what the test measures.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
79

When the t-Test and the Rank Test Disagree

  • On src_bytes the t-test says attacks send more: mean 82,820 bytes against 13,133. The rank test says attacks send less: median 0 against 233.
  • Both are correct on the same 125,973 rows. A few enormous transfers pull the attack mean above the normal one; most attack rows send nothing.
  • What it tells you: on a bell-shaped column the two tests agree and the choice does not matter. On a column with a tail, the choice is the answer. Check the shape first.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
80

The Two Tests Disagree, and the Means Are Why

  • The mean and the median describe the same 125,973 rows and point in opposite directions.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
81

Correlation: Do Two Numeric Columns Rise Together?

DefinitionCorrelation runs from -1 to 1. Pearson's r asks how close the points are to a straight line. Spearman's rho asks the same of the ranks, so a tail cannot fool it. Near 0, no relation. Near 1 or -1, one column predicts the other.
  • Example 1, serror_rate against srv_serror_rate: r = 0.99, rho = 0.97. The same information twice.
  • Example 2, duration against src_bytes: r = 0.07 raw and 0.10 after log1p; rho = 0.23. A long connection is barely more likely to be a big one.
  • What it says: a pair near 1 means drop one column before modelling. A pair near 0 means each carries something the other does not.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
82

Correlation, Twice on NSL-KDD

  • Six thousand sampled rows per panel; the coefficients come from all 125,973.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
83

One Says Nothing, the Other Says a Lot

  • The same two columns, measured two ways.
Why it mattersPearson asks whether the values rise together. Spearman asks whether the ranks do. On a column with a tail this long, only the second question has a usable answer.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
84

Correlation on Codes: The Right-Hand Column, Measured

  • Now that correlation has a slide: code protocol_type as tcp 0, udp 1, icmp 2 and Pearson's r against the label is 0.05. Code it icmp 0, tcp 1, udp 2 and r is -0.28. The sign and the size both changed, and nothing about the data did.
  • Chi-square on the same pair gives V = 0.282 under either coding. It counts rows in cells; it never multiplies the codes.
  • What it tells you: correlation needs amounts on both sides. On a nominal column the number it returns depends on a choice you made, so it measures your choice.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
85

Regression: Draw the Line, Read the Slope

DefinitionRegression fits a straight line through two numeric columns and reports its slope, how much the second column moves when the first moves by one, and R squared, the share of the second column's variation the line explains.
  • Example 1, log1p(dst_bytes) on log1p(src_bytes): slope 0.84, R squared 0.49. The line explains about half.
  • Example 2, srv_count on count: slope 0.30, R squared 0.22. A fifth.
  • What it says: neither column is a function of the other. And regression on the label itself is the mistake logistic regression exists to fix; that is a later lecture.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
86

Regression, Twice on NSL-KDD

  • The fitted line on a sample of 6,000 rows; the equation comes from all 125,973.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
87

Which Amount Columns to Keep

  • Keep a column whose Cliff's delta against the label is past 0.3 in either direction: count, serror_rate, logged_in's numeric cousins in the rate group. Drop num_outbound_cmds, which is constant, and hot, whose effect is 0.03.
  • When two columns have a correlation above 0.9, keep one: serror_rate and srv_serror_rate at 0.99 are one column twice. The worked example on the 15 rate columns, later in this deck, does this for the whole group.
  • Before any test that assumes a bell, transform the long tails with log1p and check the shape again.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
88

Amounts, Summed Up

  1. 1Analysis: mean, sd and shape for every amount; two-group gaps by t-test and rank test; correlations between columns.
  2. 2Issue: long tails that drag the mean, p-values that are tiny for everything, pairs of columns that repeat each other.
  3. 3Tools: the bell check, effect sizes instead of p, Spearman instead of Pearson on tails, log1p before anything that assumes a bell.
  4. 4Solution: keep amounts with Cliff's delta past 0.3, one of each correlated pair, and transform the tails. Thresholds written down: 0.3 and 0.9.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems

The Assumption Under Everything

  • Almost every model you will train assumes the data is IID.
  • The assumption is rarely stated and frequently false. The next slides test it on this dataset.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
96

IID in Plain Words, on This Dataset

DefinitionIndependent means one row tells you nothing about another. Identically distributed means every row, in both files, was produced by the same process.
  • Independent, here: knowing row 1,000 of KDDTrain+ is an attack tells you nothing about row 1,001, or about any other row.
  • Identically distributed, here: a row of KDDTest+ is drawn the same way as a row of KDDTrain+, so what you learn on one file holds on the other.
  • Both are claims about the data, so both can be tested with the data. The next four slides do.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
97

Independence, Tested on the File Order

  • If neighbouring rows were alike, the left panel would show stripes.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
98

The File Order Is Clean, So Where Is the Dependence?

  • Measured: the next row has the same label 50.3 percent of the time in file order, 50.2 if rows were independent, 50.5 after shuffling. Longest run of one label, 22 rows against 23 shuffled. Exact duplicate rows: 0.
  • So the file passes every check you can run on its order. NSL-KDD was built by shuffling and de-duplicating KDD'99, and that is the point of it.
  • The dependence hides in how the rows were made. Twenty-one columns, count through dst_host_srv_rerror_rate, are computed from the connections around each row in the original capture, so rows share their history however you shuffle them.
  • And 73 percent of rows have an exact twin on protocol, service, flag and both byte counts. Only 27 percent are alone.
Why it mattersA check on the file cannot see this. Only knowing how the rows were produced can, which is why the first question about any dataset is where it came from.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
99

Independence, Tested on the Rows Themselves

  • The same connection, thousands of times over.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
100

Where Identical Distribution Breaks

  • The training set and the test set are collected under different conditions.
  • The mix of classes changes between the two.
  • New categories appear later that did not exist earlier. Here no new service value does, and 21 new attack types do.
  • The world changes after the data was collected. This one is guaranteed in security.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
101

How To Check, With Code

  1. 1Compare class shares: train["family"].value_counts(normalize=True) against the same on test.
  2. 2Look for repeats: train.duplicated().sum().
  3. 3Compare category sets: set(test["service"]) - set(train["service"]).
  4. 4Compare one column's curve between the files: scipy.stats.ks_2samp(train[c], test[c]).
  5. 5Ask where the rows came from, and whether any group spans both splits.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems

  • The class mix moves between the two files, so identical distribution fails.

The Loop

  • Analysis: what did you measure, with which line of code.
  • Issue: what is wrong, stated as a consequence.
  • Tools: what technique answers it, and what its output means.
  • Solution: what you changed, and what you must not do again.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems

Worked Example: A Column That Says Nothing

nunique = train.nunique()
dead = nunique[nunique <= 1]
print(dead)
Result
num_outbound_cmds 1
dtype: int64
  • Issue: zero variance carries no information, and breaks correlation by dividing by zero.
  • Tools: nunique(), or var() == 0 for numeric columns.
  • Solution: drop it, decide the drop on training data, apply the same drop to test.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems

Worked Example: A Tail That Ruins Distances

  • The same column twice. On the left is what you get if you just plot it.

108

Fixing Scale Without Losing Rows

import numpy as np
for c in ["src_bytes", "dst_bytes", "duration"]:
    train[c + "_log"] = np.log1p(train[c])
    test[c + "_log"]  = np.log1p(test[c])
  • Tools: log1p handles zeros, since log(0) is undefined and these columns are full of zeros.
  • Solution: transform, then standardize using statistics fitted on training only.
Watch outFitting a scaler on the combined train and test data leaks test information into training. The score improves and the model gets worse in production.
NoteBook section 5.4, Preparing Data for Success, is the reading for scale and cleaning.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
109

Worked Example: Columns That Say the Same Thing

  • Fifteen columns end in _rate. Six of them carry nothing the other nine do not.
Why it mattersDuplicate columns do not break a model, they waste it: twice the width, twice the training time, and a coefficient split across two columns that should have been one.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems

Worked Example: A Group Too Small to Read

  • The same column, split by attack family. Read the row counts under the boxes first.
Watch outA box drawn from 52 rows will move if you collect 52 more. Report the count beside every group statistic, or someone will read a shape that is not there.

Worked Example: A Column That Is Cheating

train.groupby(train["class"].eq("normal"))["difficulty"].mean()
Result
class
False 18.57 (attacks)
True 20.32 (normal)
  • Issue: difficulty counts how many of 21 classifiers got this row right, scored after the fact. No sensor saw it.
  • Tools: for every column ask, could a sensor have observed this at the time.
  • Solution: drop it from the features. Keep it to report which rows are hard.
Definition21 is the easy end, 0 is the hard end. All 21 classifiers got that row right, 0 means none did.
NoteBook section 5.4 calls this a data quality issue.

Where the difficulty Score Came From

  • The NSL-KDD authors ran 21 trained models over every row and counted the ones that got it right.
NoteThe score comes from 7 learners trained 3 times each, from Tavallaee, Bagheri, Lu and Ghorbani, A Detailed Analysis of the KDD CUP 99 Data Set, the paper that built NSL-KDD.

How To Present What You Found

  1. 1State the question, then the measurement, then the number. In that order.
  2. 2Show the code that produced it, so a reader can re-run it.
  3. 3Name the consequence for the model, not just the statistic.
  4. 4Say what you changed and what you deliberately did not.
TipA result nobody can reproduce is an opinion. Your capstone is graded on whether someone else can run it and get your numbers.
